text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: INC-2026-0487 — hosted-inference: request-latency > 2s across us-west-2 pool. Priority: P1.

pagerduty-bot: Notification: primary on-call paged: @oncall-jamie (severe latency).

oncall-jamie: acked via PagerDuty. looking now — grabbing charts.

sre-marta: @oncall-jamie saw any trace IDs? I can tail the app logs for spikes.

oncall-jamie: nothing in traces yet, histogram shows 95p jump starting ~2m ago. linking dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/inf-latency

incident-bot: PagerDuty: primary on-call did not acknowledge within 120s. Escalating to secondary: @sre-marta. Manager escalation: @eng-ryan.

pagerduty-bot: Secondary paged: @sre-marta; Manager paged: @eng-ryan.

sre-marta: acked. joining. first guess: batching backlog or a GPU host flapping in the pool. pulling host health now.

ops-ana: jumping in — I see one host in us-west-2 reporting OOM kills around the time of the spike, host i-0a1b2c3d4e. CPU fine but oom_kill_count incremented.

eng-ryan: acked. if that's an OOM causing queueing, we should route traffic away from that host and scale up the pool. can we drain it?

ops-ana: draining now: ```kubectl cordon node i-0a1b2c3d4e && kubectl drain node i-0a1b2c3d4e --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data```

support-liz: customer impact check — support console shows a few 504s for enterprise customers on us-west-2 in the last 5m. Severity: elevated but not full outage. notifying top-5 affected accounts.

oncall-jamie: running quick KV cache clear on affected model variant to unblock stuck sessions: ```curl -X POST https://internal-api/kvcache/clear -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","region":"us-west-2"}'```

pagerduty-bot: Escalation note: secondary acknowledged but did not respond within 90s to the initial DM; manager has been paged as fallback.

sre-marta: I'm seeing a hotspot — one worker process is leaking memory on the model runner. OOMs are causing requests to queue on remaining workers. temp mitigation: reduce concurrency on that node's pods and spin up one extra replica in the pool.```kubectl set resources deployment/runner --limits=memory=6Gi --replicas=6```

eng-ryan: approve the temp scale (+1 replica) and a config rollback if needed. we should also consider routing policy fallback to the cheaper, smaller-model variant if latency persists.

ops-ana: scaled replicas to 6; cordon/drain in progress. metrics show 95p latency falling back toward baseline within 2m.

support-liz: updating customers: sent initial notification to affected customer list with estimated recovery.

oncall-jamie: quick sanity check on request queue depth: ```redis-cli -h redis-queue info | grep blocked_clients``` shows backlog decaying.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: escalation timeline recorded. primary ack at 5123456791, secondary ack at 5123456794, manager ack at 5123456796.

pagerduty-bot: Note: escalation policy fired because primary did not resume handling within 2m. Policy behaved as configured.

sre-marta: we're still watching for regressions. I've pushed a short-lived fix to avoid the leak and will open a follow-up PR to add more robust memory guards.

eng-ryan: good. next steps: root cause tracking (memory leak in model runner process), postmortem owner: @sre-marta, timeline draft by EOD. Can we confirm no data loss?

ops-ana: no persisted data loss; only request retries and a few 504s. logs retained at s3://redwood-logs/incidents/INC-2026-0487 for audit.

support-liz: customers acknowledged resolution messages, some asked for postmortem. adding them to distribution list.

oncall-jamie: resolving in PD: put incident in "mitigated" state, moving to follow-up. Thanks everyone for fast ops. :tada:

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident INC-2026-0487 marked mitigated by @oncall-jamie.

eng-ryan: quick retro notes in thread: 1) escalation worked but secondary response latency needs improvement, 2) runbook step for reducing concurrency should be added to hosted-inference runbook, 3) add alert to catch memory leak pattern earlier (OOM frequency > 1/min). assigning follow-ups.

sre-marta: will take postmortem, link when ready. putting a temporary guard on the runner config to prevent automatic scheduling of >6 threads per process.

support-liz: I'll send the customer post-incident summary once draft is up.

ops-ana: all nodes healthy, draining completed. monitoring for 30m then close.

oncall-jamie: last check: 95p latency back to normal, no more OOMs in last 10m. closing thread in 30. :white_check_mark:
